meta.phase: Phase 0 — Positioning, Landscape Sweep & Competitive Deep Dive

evidence_grading.1: Primary — government publications, official statistics, official pricing pages, statutes, our own interviews/pilot data
evidence_grading.2: High-quality secondary — IIM/IIIT research, established consulting, World Bank/OECD, peer-reviewed
evidence_grading.3: Market intelligence — Tracxn, Crunchbase, Factly/Dataful, SaaS directories (G2, Capterra, GetApp)
evidence_grading.4: Community — vendor blogs, LinkedIn, Reddit, YouTube, review-site excerpts

reliability_markers.VERIFIED: read directly from a primary source
reliability_markers.NOT_PUBLIC: gated behind login or sales call
reliability_markers.UNVERIFIED: could not be confirmed; do not cite externally

records.decision: Organise research by type of evidence, not by phase.
records.evidence: A claim gathered in Phase 9 and a claim gathered in Phase 20 must land in the same place if they prove the same thing. todo.md is already the phase map; duplicating it as the folder taxonomy creates two competing sources of truth that drift.
records.reverses_if: The 34 phases are later reordered such that phase number becomes the only meaningful retrieval key.

records.decision: Do NOT freeze the beachhead customer in Phase 0. Examine all segments equally and in parallel. Narrowing happens at the end, from evidence.
records.evidence: todo.md Phase 0 asks for a frozen beachhead. But the segment census shows candidate segments differ by roughly three orders of magnitude - 1,289 universities vs 48,246 colleges vs 160+ DST TBIs. Choosing before competitor and margin evidence exists would be premature. User explicitly directed research in all directions first.
records.reverses_if: Evidence shows one segment is unserviceable (no budget, no data access, or fully pre-empted).
records.status: Active - intentionally diverges from todo.md Phase 0; deviation recorded so it is not mistaken for an oversight

records.decision: Run competitor research inside Phase 0, not at Phase 9.
records.evidence: todo.md itself states competitor research 'needs to be one of your highest-priority workstreams, not something we do at the end'. Confirmed empirically: LabelNest Orbit, IncubatX and EcoSync already sell institution-facing incubation software at Rs 75k-6L/yr with India-specific government-scheme coverage. A V1 scope frozen without knowing this would have been wrong on arrival.

records.decision: The core structural finding: mandated systems are compliance ledgers, not systems of record. Anchor the positioning hypothesis on a category error in Indian innovation policy digitisation, not a missing feature inside an existing product.
records.evidence: Each mandated system has a different unit of record, none of them 'a venture, over time': IIC = the activity/event (16+/yr, each a form with 2 photos, a video URL, participant counts, one expenditure line); YUKTI = the innovation snapshot; NIRF = the spreadsheet row; AISHE = the institution-year aggregate; DPIIT = the recognition certificate. Sharpest proof: the IIC portal has a menu item called 'IPR/TTO Centres' that registers a TTO's existence and floor area - and has no field anywhere to record a single patent (GOV-022). Meanwhile NIRF demands patent commercialisation and income figures (GOV-028) and ARIIA demands patent application number and year (GOV-032), so institutions maintain a separate, off-platform patent ledger purely to answer two government screens.
records.reverses_if: A mandated system is found that does model ventures over time. MAARG comes closest (GOV-041) but is scoped to DPIIT-recognised startups, not institutional portfolios - re-verify before revisiting.

records.decision: Treat IPR lifecycle management, TRL-as-a-first-class-object, and YUKTI-NIR/IIC/ARIIA export as the strategic core of the differentiation hypothesis.
records.evidence: Across 11 direct competitors, not one has an IPR module. The only two traces in the entire market are a data field in a Swedish product (Incu) and a dashboard tile in IncubatX. Three government requirements make them unavoidable: YUKTI-NIR bands every submission by TRL and routes to different national programmes (GOV-023); ARIIA asks for 'Stage of Innovation (TRL Stage)' (GOV-032); MeitY's playbook mandates TRL benchmarking plus IP due diligence including freedom-to-operate and distinguishing ownership from a 2-year university tech-transfer licence (GOV-038). Every competitor tracks 'stage' as free text; nobody models TRL as a reportable, government-alignable object.
records.reverses_if: A competitor ships an IPR module. Given 6 of 11 vendors have zero third-party reviews and no named Indian institutional customers, low risk for ~12 months - but re-check before any external launch.

records.decision: Treat LabelNest Orbit Launch at Rs 75,000/year all-in as the number that will appear in StartupHub's competitive deals. Keep Incubatee's Rs 3,95,200 year-one as the upper reference. Do NOT build the financial model on the Rs 1.2L assumption carried in todo.md.
records.evidence: COMP-001 (Orbit Launch Rs 75k / Starter Rs 99k / Growth Rs 1.25L / Scale Rs 2.5L) and COMP-004 (Incubatee Rs 3,95,200 year one). The Rs 50k-Rs 1.2L band in todo.md is anchored above the cheapest credible Indian incumbent.
records.reverses_if: Phase 8 pricing research or Phase 3 interviews establish a validated different price point. Until then Rs 75k is a COMPETITIVE anchor, not a pricing decision.
records.status: Active - CRITICAL CAVEAT: LabelNest publishes two conflicting Orbit price lists on its own domain (institutional tiers vs 'Orbit OS Rs 29,999/month'). In a procurement-comparison conversation where that surfaces, StartupHub wins on transparency.

records.decision: Do not create a new budget line. Position against the IIC grant, the DST/NIDHI grant, or an Atal Incubation Centre allocation.
records.evidence: The decision-maker is typically a single nodal officer or IIC coordinator with no budget line of their own (COMP-024, COMP-025). India's compliance burden is already extreme - 'a typical firm has to navigate around 1,500 Acts which collectively impose 69,233 separate compliances and 6,618 independent filings' (COMP-028). A tool that reads as MORE compliance is dead on arrival; a tool that REDUCES re-keying into existing mandated portals has a strong pitch. Verified YUKTI-NIR innovations auto-pool into ARIIA Section 4 ranking (GOV-024), so a product that improves an institution's national ranking sells into a budget line that already exists.
records.reverses_if: Phase 19 GTM research finds a dedicated institutional innovation-software budget line at a material number of institutions.

records.decision: Pricing floor stays above the free-tier anchors (Trello ~Rs 54k/yr at 10 users, Notion Plus ~Rs 86k/yr at 8 editors, ClickUp ~Rs 76k/yr). Differentiate on being the only thing that produces a compliant submission, not on cost.
records.evidence: COMP-017, COMP-020, COMP-001. The most dangerous pricing neighbourhood is Notion/Airtable/Coda at 8 editors - all inside or just below the Rs 50k-Rs 5L band - and all three gate audit logs behind Enterprise (COMP-017, COMP-019). Notion's audit log records events only 'starting from the time of upgrade', with NO retroactive history (COMP-031). Institutions need retroactive audit trails for accreditation and grant audits. That is a hard, citable, structural barrier.
records.reverses_if: Phase 8 reveals institutions genuinely cannot pay above Rs 50k/yr, in which case a deliberately thinner, cheaper product is required - but it would have to accept losing the audit-trail differentiator.

records.decision: Log negative research findings as findings. 'We searched and found nothing' is written into the record with the scope of the search.
records.evidence: Three negative findings materially change the work: no public API exists for IIC, YUKTI, NIRF, AISHE or MAARG (GOV-043); no Indian campus ERP vendor has a startup-incubation module (COMP-021); and no peer-reviewed literature quantifies Indian institutional reporting burden (OQ-12). Each removes a build-vs-buy option or opens a gap, and each would otherwise be re-researched every phase.

records.decision: The biggest single sale blocker is migration, so migration must be a product. Guaranteed, free-or-subsidised migration - explicitly including WhatsApp group to structured records - is a Phase 20 pilot requirement and a Phase 22 build decision, not a customer service courtesy.
records.evidence: In Indian incubators the WhatsApp group IS the operational database (COMP-024 - IISc's own IIC links students to a WhatsApp group). Incu (Sweden) is the only vendor in the entire research stating it will import existing data at onboarding. Nobody has productised migration from open-question forms and spreadsheets. Migrating a university's data out of those is the #1 real blocker to any sale and is manual, unpaid work the BUYER would otherwise do.
records.reverses_if: Phase 12 feature-gap research finds a migration tool already commoditised.

records.decision: Watch item: BHASKAR may become the national master data layer. StartupHub's data model must be designed so it can reconcile to BHASKAR IDs rather than duplicate them. Do not build a proprietary startup identity.
records.evidence: DPIIT has reportedly planned an overhaul of BHASKAR into a 'National Startup Master Data' registry that would unify records and track the startup lifecycle, with MeitY Startup Hub floating a similar tender (GOV-040). CONFIDENCE: LOW - trade-press reporting of a plan, not a published notification.
records.reverses_if: No tender or notification materialises within ~18 months. Re-verify before any external communication; do not cite this externally until confirmed from a government source.

records.decision: Ignore hallucinated vendor claims; the market is full of them. Self-reported metrics, customer testimonials and award badges are Tier 4 unless independently corroborated.
records.evidence: Specific flags recorded: Gohorto's 'G2 High Performer 2026' badge rests on 3 reviews, one vendor-referred, with self-authored comparison pages rating itself 4.8 and every rival 2.1-3.6 (COMP-009); IncubatX's 'SOC 2-ready' is not SOC 2 (COMP-005); Incubatee claims no GST/TDS/UPI despite being an Indian vendor; and four names on the original watchlist (Applied, Bezu, Value Design Lab, Gobi) DO NOT EXIST as incubator software (COMP-016). Multiple vendors in this category serve AI-generated SEO content as their entire published feature set.
records.reverses_if: Independent verification becomes available for any specific claim.
